blocks.text: What makes a good domain name?

content.text: A domain name does four jobs at once. It is the address customers type, the name they say out loud, the text they see in a search result, and the first part of your business email. A good name is short enough to remember, easy enough to spell after hearing it once, and close enough to your business name that nobody has to guess the connection.

Try the phone test before you commit. Read the name once to a friend over the phone and ask them to type it. If they spell it right without asking you to repeat it, the name passes. If they hesitate, ask about a spelling, or add a hyphen you did not mention, keep looking. Most of the names that fail this test are too long, use an unusual spelling, or mix words that sound alike.
Choosing a name is only the first half of the job. Once the name is yours, it still needs a website behind it. If you have not picked hosting yet, read
how much web hosting costs in Pakistan
first, then come back and register the name.

blocks.text: Start with your business name, not a keyword list

content.text: The simplest choice is usually the best: your business name, exactly as customers know it. If your shop is called Ahmed Electronics, ahmedelectronics.com or ahmedelectronics.pk is the name to try first. Consistency between your shop sign, your Facebook page, and your domain builds recognition, and customers who already know the business do not have to learn a second name.

Keyword-stuffed names look clever and age badly. A name like BestCheapMobileAccessoriesLahore.com is hard to say, hard to type on a phone, and looks like a spam site in a search result. A short brandable name is easier to put on a business card, a shop sign, and a WhatsApp status, and it still works if the business adds a new product line next year.

If your exact business name is taken, add one short relevant word, not three. A city, a trade word, or pk usually does it, for example ahmedelectronicslahore.com or ahmedelectronicspk.com. Keep the result short enough to pass the phone test, and check it the same way before you buy.

blocks.text: .com, .pk or .com.pk: which ending fits your business?

content.text: For a Pakistani business this is the first real decision after the name itself, and there is no single right answer. It depends on who you sell to.

rows.text: Businesses that may sell outside Pakistan
The most recognised ending in the world. Short names are often taken, so keep two or three backups ready.
Businesses whose customers are only in Pakistan
A clear local signal. PKNIC requires a 2-year minimum term, and the registry fee is Rs 2,100 per year.
Local shops and companies that want a Pakistan signal
Check the price on the domain search page
The commercial ending under .pk. A practical fallback when the .com and the .pk of your name are both taken.

blocks.text: How to shortlist and check a name in 5 steps

content.text: Work through the steps in order, and do not skip the checks. A name that looks good on paper can fail the moment a real customer tries to type it.

items.text: Write down 5 to 10 candidates.
Start with your business name, then add a city or a short trade word for the ones that are taken.
Say each one out loud.
Drop any name that needs spelling out, and drop any name with a hyphen or a number.
Check availability for all three endings.
Search the .com, the .pk, and the .com.pk of each candidate on the
domain search page
, because one of them is often taken and that alone can settle the choice.
Check the name on social media too.

If your Facebook page or Instagram handle uses a different spelling, customers will get confused. A matching name across your domain and your social pages is worth a small compromise on the domain itself.
Register the winner the same day.
Good names get taken while you think about them. If the budget allows, register the second ending too and point it at the same website, so every reasonable guess leads to your site.

blocks.text: 6 mistakes Pakistani businesses make with domain names

content.text: Most bad domain names fail in the same few ways. Avoid these and the name will serve the business for years.

items.text: Picking a name that is hard to spell in English.
Many Pakistani business names have more than one common spelling, and customers will try the one they know.
Using hyphens or numbers to get the exact name.
A hyphen is easy to forget and a number makes people guess whether to type the digit or the word.
Choosing a name that only fits today.
A name tied to one city or one product becomes a problem when the business grows past it.
Registering the domain in someone else's name.
The domain should be registered in the business owner's name with the owner's email, so renewal notices and transfer control stay with the business.
Forgetting the renewal date.
A lapsed domain can take a live website and business email offline within days, so enable auto-renewal and keep the contact email current.
Buying the domain and forgetting the website.
A domain is only an address. Without hosting and a site behind it, customers reach an empty page.
